<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="סיון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918679_theRebbe_674" batchId="meluket-_D7_A1_D7_99_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918679_theRebbe_674__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the date and occasion for the maamar, the eve of Shavuos 5749.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">The night of the 5th of Sivan,</t>
    <t s="2">the eve of the holiday of Shavuos,</t>
    <t s="3">5749*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the famous question of why the first commandment mentions the Exodus from Egypt rather than the creation of heaven and earth, which is a greater wonder.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"I am Hashem your G-d, Who brought you out of the land of Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="1">This verse is the first utterance of the Ten Commandments given at the giving of the Torah on the 6th of Sivan,</t>
    <t s="2">after Yisrael preceded "we will do" to "we will hear"</t>
    <t s="3">[and ministering angels came and tied two crowns to each Jew, one corresponding to "we will do" and one corresponding to "we will hear"]</t>
    <t s="4">on the 5th of Sivan.</t>
    <t s="5">And it is brought in several discourses of our Nesi'im,</t>
    <t s="6">the well-known question of the great ones of Yisrael,</t>
    <t s="7">Behold, the creation of heaven and earth is a greater wonder than the Exodus from Egypt.</t>
    <t s="8">For in the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="9">even though there were several miracles,</t>
    <t s="10">behold, in addition to this not being a sufficient explanation for why it specifically says "Who brought you out of the land of Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="11">since also before the Exodus from Egypt and after the Exodus from Egypt there were so many miracles,</t>
    <t s="12">the matter of a miracle is a change from existence to existence,</t>
    <t s="13">but the creation of heaven and earth is existence from nothingness.</t>
    <t s="14">And in addition to this that creation of existence from nothingness is a greater wonder,</t>
    <t s="15">behold also the G-dly power in creation of existence from nothingness is a more elevated power,</t>
    <t s="16">as is known</t>
    <t s="17">that creation of existence from nothingness is only through the power of the Awtsmoos, whose existence is from His own essence.</t>
    <t s="18">[And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="19">that the fact that the existence of the created existence is true existence,</t>
    <t s="20">is because its coming into being is from the Awtsmoos,</t>
    <t s="21">the true existence].</t>
    <t s="22">And why does it say "Who brought you out of the land of Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="23">for ostensibly it should have said "Who created heaven and earth."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that both creation and the giving of the Torah are from the Awtsmoos, renewed every moment, connecting the Exodus to the essence of the Giver.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And one may add,</t>
    <t s="2">that this, that ostensibly it should have said "Who created heaven and earth,"</t>
    <t s="3">is also because the creation of heaven and earth and the giving of the Torah</t>
    <t s="4">("I am Hashem your G-d" is the opening of the giving of the Torah)</t>
    <t s="5">are related to each other.</t>
    <t s="6">For the creation of heaven and earth is renewed every single moment,</t>
    <t s="7">according to the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov on the verse,</t>
    <t s="8">"Forever, Hashem, Your word stands firm in the heavens"</t>
    <t s="9">(brought in the holy Tanya)</t>
    <t s="10">that the G-dly power constantly brings the created being into existence from nothingness to existence.</t>
    <t s="11">And since creation and coming into being of existence from nothingness is through the power of the Awtsmoos,</t>
    <t s="12">it is understood,</t>
    <t s="13">that the creation that is in every single moment is actual existence from nothingness from the Awtsmoos.</t>
    <t s="14">And similarly regarding the Torah,</t>
    <t s="15">that its giving</t>
    <t s="16">(and its drawing down)</t>
    <t s="17">is from the Awtsmoos</t>
    <t s="18">("Anochi" — I am),</t>
    <t s="19">and its drawing down from the Awtsmoos is in every moment,</t>
    <t s="20">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="21">"He gives the Torah" in the present tense,</t>
    <t s="22">therefore our sages said,</t>
    <t s="23">"Every day,</t>
    <t s="24">they shall be in your eyes as new,"</t>
    <t s="25">literally new.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
